title: Guest Docker workloads, recursive VMs and host isolation
objective: Give a directly running guest agent ordinary Docker/Compose control for arbitrary project test services and recursive Little Mester VMs where nested virtualization is supported, while the outer VM continues to isolate the host and the existing egress allowlist/no-host-route policy remains enforced.

acceptance_criteria.text: From the guest agent, bring up a representative project Compose stack (including PostgreSQL), run its tests, stop/restart services, and tear down the stack without requiring host Docker or host-side compose orchestration.

Guest-local ports, bind mounts within the selected guest workspace, volumes and ordinary Compose features work for guest workloads; no generated restrictive compose overlay silently blocks normal project behavior.

Host isolation remains intact: no host Docker socket, no host route/LAN exposure, no access to host files outside the selected workspace, and no host credential directory mount. Services do not publish onto the host LAN.
The existing QEMU restrict=on and approved HTTP(S) egress allowlist remain enforced for guest and workload traffic; do not widen policy or add a relay without evidence and owner approval.

When nested virtualization is available, the guest can launch and control a nested Little Mester VM with an explicitly selected guest-side workspace, run a test there, and stop it. Capability absence is detected and reported without weakening the outer boundary.
Lifecycle distinguishes ordinary guest workload cleanup from outer-VM deletion; it does not silently delete active recursive test state or evidence, and any destructive teardown is explicit.
Tests cover Compose feedback loops, host-boundary negative cases, current egress allow/deny policy and nested-VM capability/boot behavior; evidence is recorded before claiming support.

needed: credential-forwarding boundary test: no host secret directory mount and no credential when disabled
selected cloud provider auth works only when its required egress is allowed
Guest loopback service reachability and no host-LAN publication
Current egress allow/deny matrix without policy widening
Nested VM boot/test/stop and unsupported-host behavior
Outer VM teardown confirmation and nested-state/evidence handling

VM model API forwarder boundary check coordinated with #42: host Docker version >=28, host publishes only 127.0.0.1:8080/11434, separate LAN host cannot connect, guest can reach only configured forwarded model APIs, and QEMU restrict=on remains set. Do not broaden networking or expose ports on 0.0.0.0.

Existing entries preserved; public-only proxy enforcement unchanged; no allow-all or provider domains granted. #41 build fix loads CLI/auth-helper proxy env separately from daemon/RUN arguments; live registry build retry still pending.
